name: CCU — User Centered Design
tagline: Fostering Ecological Awareness Through Legible, Everyday Tangible Computing
introduction: A 7-week academic design research project exploring how tangible and ubiquitous computing can make ecological footprints visible, meaningful, and actionable within local community environments.

background.title: Project Background
background.subtitle: Addressing the invisibility of ecological impacts in ubiquitous digital services.
paragraphs: In contemporary connected environments, the ecological weight of digital and material consumption remains largely abstract. While connected appliances, smart campuses, and digital services proliferate, their ambient resource demands—from water and electricity to raw material extraction—are hidden behind frictionless interfaces.

This project investigates the critical gap between computational convenience and environmental responsibility. By situated interaction design, we examine how physical, ambient, and situated computing can bridge this rift without inducing cognitive fatigue or moralistic guilt.

Grounding our inquiry in Sustainable Interaction Design (SID) principles, we explore interaction paradigms that foster long-term stewardship, collective awareness, and deliberate material engagement over ephemeral convenience.

objectives.title: Goals & Objectives
objectives.subtitle: Structured deliverables guiding our research, conceptualization, and prototype evaluation.

items.title: Contextual Inquiry & Resource Mapping
items.description: Conduct situated observational studies and semi-structured interviews across shared campus workspaces to trace invisible resource flows.
items.deliverable: Situational Journey Maps & Resource Friction Audit

items.title: Legible Interface Conceptualization
items.description: Synthesize design opportunities into ambient and tangible feedback mechanics that communicate ecological consequences without interrupting everyday tasks.

items.title: Physical Computing Prototyping
items.description: Engineer functional low-power hardware mockups utilizing modular components, bio-materials, and legible physical motion to convey ecological metrics.

items.title: Participatory Evaluation & Open Toolkit
items.description: Validate the prototype with campus stakeholder cohorts over a multi-day deployment, documenting behavioral reflections and publishing an open SID toolkit.
items.deliverable: Comprehensive Research Report & Open Design Spec

outcomes.title: Expected Outcomes
outcomes.subtitle: Tangible artifacts and research contributions anticipated by week seven.

cards.title: Evaluative Research Paper
cards.description: Rigorous academic documentation analyzing user perceptions, ethical dilemmas, and longitudinal interaction shifts.

cards.title: Open SID Design Repository
cards.description: Publicly shared CAD files, firmware, schematics, and design guidelines for academic and open-source replication.
